26: This is the correct version: Here is when the [knife is] descending in front of him and ascending behind him. Here is when the upward motion is in front of him but the downward motion is behind him. Here is when the downward motion is both in front of him and behind him. And here is when the upward motion is both in front of him and behind him. Any [incident resulting from an] upward motion  is exempt and any [incident resulting from a] downward motion is liable. Therefore, that which was taught "before him, he is liable, behind him is exempt" is referring to [a scenario where] the downward motion was in from of him and the downward motion was behind him, viz. he lowered his arm in order to [then] lift it with force. [So now] when he lifts it with force [if he kills] when lowering in front of him he is liable, [but] if he killed when lifting it behind him he would be exempt. And that which was taught "behind him, he is liable, in front of him, he is exempt" is referring to [a scenario where] the upward motion was in front of him and the downward motion was behind him, e.g. one who lifts his hand with force to the point where it [the ax] was lowered behind him over his shoulders, and then reverses [the motion] to lift [his hands[ to strike in front of him. [So now] if he kills when he was lowering it behind him he is liable, [but if] he killed when he was lifting it [back] he is exempt]. And that which was taught "whether in front of him and behind him, he is liable" is referring to the downward motion, whether it was before him or behind him. And that which was taught "Whether it was in front of him or behind him, he is exempt" is referring to the upward motion, whether it was before or behind him.
